question: What keeps a too-weak unit off an enemy's ground in the route, what stops a country attacking out of a neutral it only has transit through, and the unit-arrived message: its type, when, for whom, with what.

addresses.name: CPathFind::MayStep
addresses.revises: comment and confidence: read on the listing, the step's tests in order with the stand-in test and the shatter test the old comment left out, the last test named (military access out of a neutral), the four land tests asked of a land unit only; inferred -> confirmed
addresses.signature: bool __thiscall CPathFind::MayStep(CPathFind* this, CUnit* unit, CProvince* goal, CProvince* from, CProvince* to, ProvinceEdge* edge)
addresses.comment: CPathFind slot 2: whether `unit` may step from `from` to `to` along `edge`, with `goal` the search's destination (which the base ignores and both safe finders use). `this` is not read; `ret 0x14` covers the five stack arguments. In order: no for an edge of kind 3, for `from == to`, for `goal`'s template flag +0x13D clear, and where IsCrossingBlocked (rva 0x1A2600) closes the edge. A fleet: land to land never; sea to land only into the land province whose +0xA4 names `from`; land to sea only into the sea `from`'s +0xA4 names, and yes outright there where slot 34 refuses `from` (a fleet puts out of a port it may no longer lie in). Then **slot 34 (MayStandIn) with `to`** - no where it says no. **A non-land unit is done (yes).** A land unit stepping into a province whose controller (+0x338) is not its owner (+0x128) faces four more, each by the owner: (1) IsEnemyTag(country[to.controller], &owner) (rva 0x2F1B0, REB counted) and strength x 1000 / GetTotalStrengthCeiling (slot 24) below CUnit::ShatterThreshold - ceiling 0 counts as -1 - no: **a unit too weak to hold is never routed onto enemy ground**, the same test CUnit::CanMoveTo makes; (2) the same IsEnemyTag, supply_received_percentage (+0xFC) 0 and CUnit::SupplyConsumption > 0: no; (3) CUnit::FuelConsumption > 0, the same IsEnemyTag and fuel_received_percentage (+0x100) 0: no; (4) the owner's CDiplomacyStatus for `from`'s controller has hasMilitaryAccess (+0x4C), IsEnemyTag(country[from.controller], &to.controller) is false, and the owner's status for `to`'s controller has a war (+0x20): no - **a country cannot attack out of a neutral that merely lets it through**. Yes otherwise. Every finder calling the base (plain, CSafePathFind, CVerySafePathFind) asks all of it, so it binds the player's orders and the AI's alike; CPlannedPathFind does not call the base. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, sections 3 and 12.1.

Shown wrong by a different register binding of from/to - the arguments are ebp+8 unit, +0xC goal, +0x10 from, +0x14 to, +0x18 edge.

addresses.name: CUnit::CanMoveTo
addresses.revises: comment only: every test in order, read whole, where the old comment listed the shatter test alone; and that the click asks it and the command does not
addresses.comment: **Whether this unit may be sent to that province**, virtual slot 35 (CUnit, CArmy and CNavy share the body; CAir overrides it to gate on cloud and then tail-calls this). In order: no unless slot 34 (MayStandIn) says yes; no where a land unit at sea is sent to land that has no edge to its province (CProvinceTemplate::HasEdgeTo); no where it has battles and its CanRetreatToProvince slot refuses the province. A land unit: no where CCountry::IsEnemy(country[province.controller], &owner, province) (the province form, rva 0x2F210 - an undeclared war covering the province counts) and its strength over GetTotalStrengthCeiling is under CUnit::ShatterThreshold; no where it is carried by no fleet (CArmy +0x300 == 0), IsEnemy(..., province), supply_received_percentage 0 and SupplyConsumption > 0; no where FuelConsumption > 0, IsEnemy(..., province) and fuel_received_percentage 0. Every unit: no where it has a path, battles, and a battle in the next province of its path (HasCombatIn). Yes for anything but a fleet; a fleet yes where the province is SeaConnected to its own sea (its province, or the sea its port names) and one of its ships (CNavy +0x2E4 list) has +0x140 above nought. **It is the click's test** (CUnit::OrderToProvince: a refusal is the illegal_selection_projection and the error sound), not CMoveCommand::Execute's; the route (CPathFind::MayStep) then asks the same shatter, supply and fuel tests of every step with the tag form of IsEnemy and without the carried unit's exemption. So the shatter threshold does two jobs: below it a unit shatters when hurt, and below it a unit is neither sent nor routed into enemy ground. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-shatter.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 12.2.

addresses.name: CUnit::AnnounceArrival
addresses.revises: comment only: the air unit is told only at its own base, the message's variables, province, countries and unit, its Goto, and both call sites in AdvanceMovement with the halted-on-arrival and boarding cases
addresses.comment: Posts the message that a unit has arrived. Nothing unless the unit's owner id (+0x128) is the game state's player id; it is a land unit (slot 15) or a fleet (slot 16), **or an air unit whose home base object answers (its slot 0) the province it is in** - an air unit is told only at its own base; and it has no order or its order's type id is none of 0x42E patrol, 0x6E9 convoy raid, 0x6E8 convoy escort. Type UNITARRIVED_LAND, UNITARRIVED_NAVAL or UNITARRIVED_AIR by kind (CMessageHandler::FindType). Variables: CCountry::BuildMessageVariables of the player's country, then MESSENGER = the text of MESSAGE_HEAD_MARS, NAME = the unit's GetName, PROV = its current province's name, TYPE = the rendered text of ARMY, NAVY or EXP_SQUADRON. CMessage::CMessage with the current province, an empty head string, the player's tag and id as both countries and the unit's type and id last; posted through PostMessage_CMessageHandler with CMessageHandler::GotoUnitForMessage. Called twice by CUnit::AdvanceMovement, both in the arrival branch: on boarding a fleet (0x5CAD61) where the path's last node after the pop is the sea boarded, before the unit leaves the shore; and at the common tail (0x5CB13E) when the unit has no battles and no path left - which is reached after an ordinary entry, after boarding, and after the arm where slot 34 no longer allows the province and CancelMovement empties the path, so a unit halted on arrival is told it arrived where it was halted. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, sections 5 and 12.3.
